text.p: Colombian stocks ended mixed on Tuesday as new technology failed to revive investor interest.
The Medellin exchange followed the example set by Bogota on Monday and switched to the silent, electronic dealing system, which has hushed live trading floors.

Medellin's IBOMED index edged up a wafer-thin 0.02 percent to close at 13,628.37 on a volume of 693 million pesos. Bogota's IBB index eased 0.21 percent to 867.62 on a 2.3 billion pesos trading volume.
"Dealing is returning to normal after the introduction of the new trading system. But despite the speed the new system offers, investors are still apathetic," one Bogota broker said.
The flotation of satellite communications company Colomsat was the main focus of interest on the Bogota exchange. Its shares closed at 4,400 pesos each on a 1.2 billion peso trading volume.

"This was the first day of trading in Colomsat shares in Bogota although it was registered last week," a Bogota broker said. The IBB index was dragged down by a 4.1 percent fall to 418 pesos in Banco de Colombia shares and a 0.83 percent drop to 5,930 in Banco de Bogota shares.

"Banco de Bogota shareholder started to take profits given that the price hit 6,000 pesos and could not be sustained. Investors preferred to sell before the price dropped," another broker said. "Banco de Colombia shareholders had been expecting a bumper dividend payout but when that failed to materialize they sold."

The falls in the two banks were offset by gains in cement manufacturer Cementos Caribe, part of the Sindicato Antioqueo industrial conglomerate. Its shares moved up 3.72 percent to 4,200 pesos on a volume of 141.3 million pesos. -- Javier Mozzo, Bogota newsroom, 571 6107544
